Logically it contradicts the immediately following sentence, which demotes the laboratory to 'only one stage in its construction' — the blank must name something beyond the lab, not the lab itself. Also echoes the rejected individualist rhetoric ('discoveries are made in laboratories').

Logically entailed by the two governing premises: (i) 'knowledge isn't knowledge unless it has been authorized by disciplinary specialists' — a collective body; (ii) 'What happens in somebody's laboratory is only one stage in its construction' — 'construction' anaphorically requires a constructed artifact, i.e., a 'product', built in multiple stages by multiple agents, i.e., 'collective'. Both long-distance cues converge uniquely on this option.

'Unbiased' belongs to the individualist rhetoric under critique ('an inquiring but unbiased mind'), and 'impression' denotes a subjective, individual mental state — the opposite of communal authorization. 'A truth becomes an unbiased impression' is also a category mismatch (truth is not an impression), and the pronoun chain 'its construction' cannot coherently refer to an impression.
